root_cause.text: The iris vb2 stop_streaming path incorrectly treated the IRIS_INST_ERROR state as a reason to skip teardown, so `iris_vb2_stop_streaming()` failed to return queued buffers and perform cleanup for errored instances.
root_cause.evidence: The reverted check in `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c` removed `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;`, and the commit message states this skip caused buffers not to be returned to vb2 and prevented proper teardown, leaving firmware in an inconsistent state.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The reverted check in `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c` removed `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;`, and the commit message states this skip caused buffers not to be returned to vb2 and prevented proper teardown, leaving firmware in an inconsistent state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow stop_streaming to run its normal cleanup even when the instance is in an error state.
intent_record.what: The early-exit check in iris_vb2_stop_streaming() that tested whether inst->state equals IRIS_INST_ERROR and jumped to the exit label was removed, leaving the function to continue executing past that point even when the instance is in the error state.
intent_record.how: At runtime, stop_streaming will no longer skip its normal shutdown logic when the instance is already marked as being in an error state. This allows the function to continue processing stream stop handling and cleanup instead of returning early, which can prevent missed teardown behavior during error conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always mark outstanding buffers as done with error during stop_streaming, while only transitioning the instance to error state when stop fails.
intent_record.what: The call to iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR) was moved out of the conditional block guarded by if (ret), so it now executes unconditionally at the exit label, while iris_inst_change_state(inst, IRIS_INST_ERROR) remains conditional on ret.
intent_record.how: At runtime, all queued buffers are now always completed with VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR when stop_streaming exits, regardless of whether ret indicates an error, while the instance state is only switched to IRIS_INST_ERROR when an actual error is reported. This ensures buffers are properly finalized even on non-error stop paths.

grouping_result.intent: Always mark outstanding buffers as done with error during stop_streaming, while only transitioning the instance to error state when stop fails.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure stop_streaming performs normal cleanup and marks pending buffers as errored even if the instance is already in an error state, only setting the instance error state when stopping itself fails.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the root cause by removing the error-state early exit in stop_streaming, ensuring teardown and queued-buffer cleanup still occur for IRIS_INST_ERROR instances, and only setting the error state when stopping fails.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the root of the bug: it treats an existing IRIS_INST_ERROR state as a reason to bypass normal stop_streaming teardown.
When reached due to the IRIS_INST_ERROR check, this jump skips the cleanup path that should return queued buffers and perform teardown for errored instances.
This makes buffer completion with error conditional on stop failure, so when stop_streaming exits early due to preexisting IRIS_INST_ERROR, outstanding buffers are not marked done.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the direct root cause: it treats an already errored instance as a reason to skip the normal stop_streaming teardown path, preventing queued buffers from being returned and cleanup from running.
Reached under the IRIS_INST_ERROR check, this jump exits stop_streaming before the cleanup path executes, causing outstanding buffers and teardown handling to be skipped for errored instances.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant logic in `iris_vb2_stop_streaming()` clearly enough to decide. The vulnerable root cause was that the stop-streaming path treated `IRIS_INST_ERROR` as a reason to skip teardown, causing queued buffers not to be returned and cleanup not to happen for errored instances. In this commit, the function now explicitly checks `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;`, but at `exit:` the cleanup is no longer unconditional. Instead, `iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);` is executed only inside `if (ret) { ... }`. Since the newly added `goto exit;` on `IRIS_INST_ERROR` does not set `ret`, the errored-instance path skips both `stream_off` and buffer return/cleanup. That means the vulnerable construct is still present: errored instances still do not have queued buffers returned. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and does not contain the fix for the stated root cause.
